sections.h2: How does a house sale work in North Chicago, Illinois?
sections.html:
A North Chicago sale runs through two layers of paperwork: the city's own transfer stamp and sale inspection, then the Lake County Clerk's recording desk. An owner can hire an agent, go it alone, or take a direct offer from a buyer willing to accept the property in its present shape.

North Chicago is a Lake County city of about 8 square miles on the Lake Michigan shore, directly south of Waukegan. The latest Census Bureau estimate, dated July 2025, is 34,050 residents, up from 30,759 counted in 2020. The Great Lakes naval training center sits inside the city, and the Census Bureau counts 2,653 veterans among residents for 2020 to 2024.

The city's rules matter more than usual for a seller. A sale cannot close with a stamped deed until the city has checked for unpaid bills and, for any building, completed a sales inspection. Starting that process early keeps a closing date from slipping.

sections.h2: What shapes a sale in North Chicago?
sections.html:
The city grew around industry and the Navy. Land speculators moved in during the 1890s, a railroad depot opened in 1892, and the Washburn and Moen barbed wire plant became the first big employer. The settlement incorporated as a village in 1895 and as a city in 1909, and the Navy created its training area in 1911. A veterans hospital followed in 1926.

The population peaked in the 1970 census at 47,275 and fell to 30,759 by 2020. A few facts shape how a house here shows:

  • North Chicago Community Unit School District 187 runs the public schools, and North Chicago High School is the city's high school.
  • Two Metra stations, North Chicago and Great Lakes, serve the Union Pacific North Line, with trains south to Chicago and north to Kenosha. Pace buses link the city to Waukegan.
  • Main roads include Sheridan Road, Green Bay Road, Waukegan Road, Skokie Highway, Buckley Road and the Tri-State Tollway.
  • Foss Park Beach on the lakefront and the Greenbelt Cultural Center and Forest Preserve are the best-known green spaces.
  • Rosalind Franklin University of Medicine and Science, home of the Chicago Medical School, is among the city's larger institutions.

Most of the city drains toward the lake, while the western edge drains to the North Branch of the Chicago River. Ask the building department about any past drainage or basement water complaints on your street before you list.

sections.h2: How many North Chicago homes are owner-held, and what are they worth?
sections.html:
Roughly one home in three is owner-held, 32.6% across the five survey years ending 2024. The table below shows the housing and income figures a seller is most likely to be asked about.

sections.h2: What steps does the city require before I can sell?
sections.html:
The city requires a transfer stamp on every sale inside its limits, and the stamp is released only after debts are cleared and the sale inspection is done. The Economic and Community Development page lays the order out this way:

  1. Call the Comptroller's Office at 847-596-8600 and the Department of Economic and Community Development at 847-596-8650 to request an outstanding payment and lien check.
  2. Pay anything the check turns up. The stamp is not issued until those payments are made.
  3. If the property has a building on it, schedule the sales inspection with Economic and Community Development.
  4. After the inspection, the buyers sign a Buyer's Acknowledgement form and give it to the Comptroller's office, which issues the stamp.
  5. The stamp goes on the deed, and the buyer or seller records the deed with the Lake County Recorder.

The department also recommends a Zoning Verification Letter before a sale. It states whether a use or structure is legal nonconforming, which can answer a buyer's questions about an old garage, an extra unit or a converted basement. The request form goes to the Economic and Community Development office at City Hall.

The building department phone is 847-596-8650, and permit questions go to permits@northchicago.org. Review times for permits are described as about 10 business days when volume is normal, so ask about timing if the inspection turns up work that needs a permit.

sections.h2: What do Illinois and Lake County charge on a deed?
sections.html:
Section 31-10 of 35 ILCS 200 sets the state tax at 50¢ for each $500 or fraction of $500. Lake County adds 25¢ per $500 on top, and its pamphlet notes that the county issues one stamp covering both. The Lake County Clerk collects the tax at recording, and the contract decides whether buyer or seller pays it.

North Chicago is one of the municipalities the county names as requiring its own stamp or exemption letter before the deed is submitted. You must get that from the city first.

  • A sale needs the Illinois Real Estate Transfer Declaration, form PTAX-203, completed through the Department of Revenue's MyDec site.
  • A deed with consideration of $100 or less carries a signed exemption statement instead of the declaration.
  • Only the stamped deed is recorded. The PTAX-203 goes to the county assessment office.
  • Recordings are filed at the Lake County Clerk's Recording Division, 18 N County St, 6th Floor, Waukegan. The office number is 847-377-2575.

The county's own pamphlet shows a $100,000 sale as an example of how the two rates combine, with a total tax of $150. Ask the Clerk's office for the figure that applies to your deed.

sections.h2: Do landlord and short-term rental rules affect a sale here?
sections.html:
Yes, if the house has ever been rented. Any dwelling not occupied by its owner falls under the landlord license rules in City Code Title 5, Chapter 14, whether or not rent is charged. The license runs January 1 to December 31, and inspections must be passed every two years for the certificate of compliance.

Other city rules that show up at closing time:

  • Short-term rentals need an endorsement on top of the landlord license, and only 25 endorsements are available per year, first come, first served.
  • Short-term rentals also owe the city's 9.5% hotel and motel tax, remitted monthly.
  • Rental properties with four or more units must have a Knox Box key box for Fire Department access under City Code Title 3, Chapter 2, Section 14.
  • Vacant and foreclosed properties must be registered through the HERA Property Registry, with a fee.
  • The city adopted the 2021 International Building, Residential, Mechanical, Fuel Gas, Fire, Property Maintenance and Existing Building codes on October 1, 2024, along with the 2020 National Electric Code.

An inherited house with a former tenant, or a house the owner has left empty, is the most common place these rules trip up a sale. Find out from the building department whether the address is registered, ideally before an offer arrives.

sections.h2: How are Lake County property taxes handled at closing?
sections.html:
Lake County sends one bill with two installment coupons. For the 2025 tax year, bills were mailed May 1, 2026, the first installment was due June 4 and the second September 4, with penalty interest added the day after each date. The county publishes a new calendar each year, and the Treasurer's office can tell you which installments are paid on your parcel.

At closing, the title company usually splits the year's tax between buyer and seller. Bring the latest bill to the closing table and phone the Lake County Treasurer if any installment shows as open. An unpaid installment stays attached to the parcel and becomes the next owner's problem unless it is settled in the closing statement.

sections.h2: Which way of selling suits a North Chicago house?
sections.html:
The choice depends on condition, timing and what the sales inspection might find. A public listing reaches the most buyers but adds showings, repair requests and a longer timeline. A direct cash sale moves faster and accepts the house with its flaws, and it still goes through the same stamp, inspection and recording steps.

  • Hire an agent and list publicly if the house shows well and you can wait for a financed buyer.
  • Sell as-is when repairs, a code violation, a former tenant or probate paperwork makes a normal listing hard.
  • Get the lien check and sales inspection started first in either case, because both can reveal debts or defects that change the price.

faqs.q: Do I need a city transfer stamp to sell in North Chicago?
faqs.a: Yes. The city requires a transfer stamp on any sale inside its limits, and it will not issue one until outstanding payments and liens are cleared and, for a building, the sales inspection is done. The stamp is attached to the deed before it is recorded.

faqs.q: Which office handles the sales inspection?
faqs.a: Call the Department of Economic and Community Development at 847-596-8650 or write to permits@northchicago.org. The Comptroller's Office at 847-596-8600 handles the lien and payment check and issues the stamp after the buyers sign the Buyer's Acknowledgement.

faqs.q: What is the Illinois and Lake County transfer tax rate?
faqs.a: Illinois takes 50¢ per $500 and Lake County takes 25¢ per $500, both collected by the Lake County Clerk when the deed is filed. The city stamp is separate, so confirm its amount with the Comptroller's Office.

faqs.q: Can I sell a North Chicago rental house with tenants in it?
faqs.a: Yes, but the unit must be covered by a landlord license, since any dwelling not occupied by its owner falls under City Code 5-14. Ask the building department for the certificate of compliance status, because a buyer or lender may want to see it.

faqs.q: Where does the deed get filed after closing?
faqs.a: Filing happens at the Lake County Clerk's Recording Division, 18 N County St, 6th Floor, Waukegan, phone 847-377-2575. The stamped deed is the document filed, while the PTAX-203 declaration is forwarded to the assessment office.
